Every result file stores its sha256, and `analyze.py` treats a file whose stored hash differs as a file problem, so an edit after the first run would make all the data unusable: the hash shows that the plan did not change after the runs.
Each job stored the sha256 of the code files it ran, and the pooled file records that none of them had changed when the jobs were pooled.
The analysis refuses smoke files as not a result, so they are never pooled and are not under `results/`.
## What the sweep cannot show
No hardware counters were read, so it cannot say where the cycles go.

The plan (`arm64/PLAN.md`) was written before the full results: its prediction held for which loops are lost and which are kept, and did not hold for "no placement effect" in the forward add and the stencil at L1; reverse and the forward add at L1 had already been timed in a smoke run when it was written, so those two statements were not blind.
A setup cost before the NEON loop is consistent with the Arm points, and the registered word is "neither".

The d-sweep timed one kernel with one compiler, read no hardware counters, and is one Arm run, so its intervals cannot show run-to-run or host-to-host spread.
